headline: High: shared filesystem and broad network/MCP surfaces create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between AutoGPT and LightAgent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT exposes filesystem and agent-protocol I/O, while LightAgent uses MCP over stdio/SSE and runtime hooks that can observe or replace lifecycle payloads. That creates a plausible bridge where one agent’s outputs can be treated as instructions by the other, even though direct default ingestion is not explicitly documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT reads LightAgent-produced files or messages as instructions
IF LightAgent forwards AutoGPT output through MCP or lifecycle hooks without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate their workspaces and temp directories
Disable automatic parsing of peer-generated files
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require human review before executing tool calls from the other agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; LightAgent has broad egress, browser access, and handles user conversations, memory, trace data, tool results, and secrets. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive data can flow from LightAgent into AutoGPT outputs or outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF LightAgent secrets or trace data are written to files AutoGPT can read
IF AutoGPT forwards those files through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Use separate OS users and directories
Block shared mounts between the agents
Redact secrets before file handoff
Restrict AutoGPT egress destinations further
Turn off verbose trace export in LightAgent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and LightAgent can also spawn subprocesses with multiple instances supported. Both therefore have overlapping write-adjacent operational authority, and if they target the same mutable workspace or git state, conflicts are plausible. No locking is documented, so uncertainty warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF either agent mutates git state without external locking
IF concurrent subprocesses touch the same artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for one agent
Snapshot the workspace before each run

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent’s tool-calling and runtime hooks can act on lifecycle payloads, while AutoGPT can generate shell actions and agent-protocol outputs. If LightAgent treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or browser actions. Because the pair can default into action-taking without a verification step, the blast radius can extend beyond a single work product.
conditions: IF LightAgent consumes AutoGPT output as task instructions
IF LightAgent executes tool calls without an explicit verification gate
IF AutoGPT emits malformed or hallucinated facts that LightAgent operationalizes
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any downstream action
Require schema checks on AutoGPT outputs
Limit LightAgent to read-only review mode
Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs
Disable autonomous execution for high-impact tasks

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool results, and secrets, while AutoGPT has filesystem and network surfaces but no stated compliance controls. If regulated data is routed through both, retention, residency, or subject-rights handling can diverge. The mismatch is plausible from the profiles alone, but not specific enough for high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in LightAgent memory or traces
IF AutoGPT persists or transmits that data outside the required jurisdiction
IF deletion or export requests must be honored across both agents
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Set short retention windows for LightAgent traces
Store data in a jurisdiction-approved location
Document deletion/export handling for both agents
Review secret-handling paths before deployment
